The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $5\sqrt{3}\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.$ Find $AC.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=5\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC, \\ m∠A & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 5\sqrt{3} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\ 5\sqrt{3} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 5\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\ 5\sqrt{3} & =\frac{5\sqrt{3}\,b}{4} \\ \cancel{5\sqrt{3}} & =\frac{\cancel{5\sqrt{3}}\,b}{4} \\ 1 & =\frac{b}{4} \\ b & =4\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=4\,\text{cm}.$

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2}{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$ Find $AC.$

The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=6\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC, \\ m∠A & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 6\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 6\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}\,b}{2} \\ \frac{21\cancel{\sqrt{2}}}{\cancel{2}} & =\frac{3\cancel{\sqrt{2}}\,b}{\cancel{2}} \\ 3b & =21 \\ b & =7\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186105904/plots/498ee40bc19fad1b0c9fe2c19553a8246386dceb0fc9c90e01fd216eee784bd5.png)

The area of the triangle $△ABC$ is $27\,\text{mm}^{2}.$ Use $\sin30^{\circ}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Find $AC.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=9\text{ mm} \\ b & =AC \\ m∠A & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{1}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 27 & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 9\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘} \\ 27 & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 9\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\ 27 & =\frac{9}{4}b \\ b & =\frac{27}{\frac{9}{4}} \\ b & =12\text{ mm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=12\,\text{mm}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186105904/plots/c8d6e6ca1f043f7d21124fe43b971f6018c9958409a33980be2a93a327c336c3.png)

The area of the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{333\sqrt{2}}{32}\,\text{mm}^{2}.$ Then, $AC=${{field-1}} $\text{mm}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=\frac{37}{4}\text{ mm} \\ b & =AC \\ m∠A & ={135}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{333\sqrt{2}}{32} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot \frac{37}{4}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘} \\ \frac{333\sqrt{2}}{32} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot \frac{37}{4}\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{333\sqrt{2}}{32} & =\frac{37\sqrt{2}}{16}b \\ b & =\frac{\frac{333\sqrt{2}}{32}}{\frac{37\sqrt{2}}{16}} \\ b & =\frac{9}{2}\text{ mm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=\frac{9}{2}\,\text{mm}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186105904/plots/963812797476a79c0b4f716867ed495383158a13c6d04e84e2dfe46623cda450.png)

The area of the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{209\sqrt{3}}{18}\,\text{mm}^{2}.$ Find $AC.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=\frac{22}{3}\text{ mm} \\ b & =AC \\ m∠A & ={120}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{209\sqrt{3}}{18} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot \frac{22}{3}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\ \frac{209\sqrt{3}}{18} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot \frac{22}{3}\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\ \frac{209\sqrt{3}}{18} & =\frac{11\sqrt{3}}{6}b \\ b & =\frac{\frac{209\sqrt{3}}{18}}{\frac{11\sqrt{3}}{6}} \\ b & =\frac{19}{3}\text{ mm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=\frac{19}{3}\,\text{mm}.$
